Notebook introduction

blocks.content: **Philosophy**: Retiam is built on the **Open-Closed Principle (OCP)**: *open for extension, closed for modification*. Adding a brand-new rendering feature, art style, physics engine, or post-processing filter must **never** require modifying core geometry, domain templates, or engine shaders.

blocks.text: 1. Overview & Architectural Manifesto
In Retiam, plugins are first-class architectural modules. When a developer writes a plugin, they are granted access to two complementary abstraction layers:

items: **High-Level Scene Graph (`Scene`)**: Entity management, animation lifecycles (`scene.always`), lighting, cameras, materials, and input events.

**Low-Level WebGPU Orchestration (`SceneComposer`)**: Direct `GPUDevice` access, GPU buffer allocation, custom compute pipelines, and dynamic [`FrameGraph`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/frame_graph/FrameGraph.ts) pass injection.

blocks.text: 2. The Core Plugin Contract (IPlugin)

All Retiam extensions — from simple config tweaks to multi-pass GPU render features — implement the single [`IPlugin`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/IPlugin.ts) interface:
Both `install()` and `registerPasses()` are optional. Implement what you need:
Installation & Dual-Level Mounting API
Plugins can be installed at either the **Scene level** (`scene.use`) or the **Composer level** (`composer.use`):
Lifecycle & Invariant Guarantees:

items: **Deduplication**: If a plugin with the same `name` is already installed, the existing instance's `dispose()` method is automatically called before the new instance is installed.
**Priority-Sorted FrameGraph Passes**: When a plugin provides `registerPasses()`, it is registered as an engine feature sorted by `priority` (lower numbers execute earlier, default is `100`).
**Chainable Fluent API**: Both `scene.use()` and `composer.use()` return `this` for fluent chaining.

blocks.text: 3. Shading Styles (Not Plugins)
Cel shading, Gooch illustration, and other material-level styles are **not plugins** — they're configuration on `RenderConfig` and `Material`:
**Rationale**: These are one-liners. Wrapping them in a plugin class adds ceremony without value.
4. The 5 Plugin Archetypes (What Plugins Can Do)

blocks.text: Archetype 1: Post-Process Pass Plugins (PostProcessPass)
These plugins intercept the final rendered presentation texture and apply screen-space fragment effects.

children: Sobel edge inking / technical contours.
HDR Bloom / Dual-kawase blur ping-pong.
Film grain, Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Color Grading LUTs.
Screen-space radial blur / motion blur.

items: **Mechanism**:

For complex multi-pass rendering pipelines requiring dedicated attachments (depth pre-passes, G-buffers, velocity vectors, shadow cascades).

children: Screen-Space Ambient Occlusion (SSAO) with bilateral depth-aware blur.
Screen-Space Reflections (SSR).
Custom depth or normal map generation.

Archetype 3: Shader & Material Extension Plugins (ShaderBuilder & WGSL Chunks)
Plugins can introduce brand-new lighting models and BRDFs without modifying `ModelFragment.ts` or `Domains.ts`.

children: Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR): Cel/Toon, Gooch CAD illustration, Clay.
Advanced materials: Subsurface Scattering (skin/wax), Iridescent thin-film (oil slicks/soap bubbles), Velvet/Cloth fuzz.
Custom procedural patterns: Wood grain, Voronoi noise, marble vein displacement.
Store the WGSL equations in `src/engine/shaders/includes/lighting/<name>.wgsl`.
`ChunkRegistry` loads them automatically.

children.text: The plugin configures the scene or injects into open pragma slots:
children: `#pragma INJECT(CUSTOM_SHADING)`: Override or blend surface reflection.
`#pragma INJECT(CUSTOM_SHADOW)`: Custom shadow filtering or penumbra shaping.
`#pragma INJECT(USER_FUNCTIONS)`: Math utilities and noise functions.

blocks.text: Archetype 4: WebGPU Compute & Simulation Plugins
Plugins can leverage `composer.device` directly to run asynchronous GPU compute shaders before rendering each frame.

children: Million-particle GPU simulations (fireworks, smoke, rain, sparks).
GPU Flocking / Boids behavior.
Spring-mass cloth or rope physics.
GPU Marching Cubes or fluid surface reconstruction.

items: **Mechanism**:

blocks.text: The plugin creates a `GPUComputePipeline`, allocates GPU storage buffers, and registers a callback via `composer` or `scene.always(...)`.

items: **Example Implementation**:

blocks.text: Archetype 5: Lifecycle, Physics & Interactive Tooling Plugins
Plugins can hook into `InteractionManager` and the frame tick loop to add interactive tools and external engines.

children: **Physics Engine Bridges**: Rapier.js / Cannon-es rigid-body integration.
**3D Transform Gizmos**: Interactive translate/rotate/scale handles in the viewport.
**Cinema Camera Rigs**: Spline-following camera dollies, camera shake dampeners.
**Exporters**: Offline MP4/WebM video rendering or GIF recording.

blocks.text: 5. Built-in Plugins & Core Engine Features
Retiam ships with several production-ready plugins and implements its own core rendering features on top of `IPlugin`:
A. [AudioPlugin](../src/engine/audio/AudioPlugin.ts) (Audio Subsystem & Web Audio Bridge)

The [`AudioPlugin`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/audio/AudioPlugin.ts) connects the [`AudioManager`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/audio/AudioManager.ts) directly into the scene graph and animation timeline:

items: **Lifecycle Synchronization**: Automatically handles scene `pause`, `resume`, `seek`, `reset`, and `timescale` (slow-motion / speed-up) events.
**Spatial 3D Audio**: Automatically attaches an `AudioListenerComponent` to `scene.camera` during frame updates so sounds pan and attenuate relative to the camera.
**Browser Autoplay Auto-Unlock**: Captures the first user interaction (`pointerdown`, `keydown`, `touchstart`, `click`) to unlock the browser's `AudioContext` without throwing DOM exceptions.

**Video Recording Hook**: Automatically wires the Web Audio destination stream into [`Recorder`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/recorder/Recorder.ts) for seamless synchronous video + audio export.
**Lazy Initialization**: Accessing `scene.audio` automatically installs `AudioPlugin` if it has not been registered yet:

blocks.text: B. [OutlinePlugin](../src/plugins/OutlinePlugin.ts) (Silhouette Inking)

The [`OutlinePlugin`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/plugins/OutlinePlugin.ts) adds real-time 8-neighbor Sobel edge detection to create Manim/technical blueprint silhouettes around 3D geometry:

items: **Self-Contained**: Implemented 100% inside `src/plugins/OutlinePlugin.ts` with zero engine core modifications.
**Custom Shader Pass**: Injects an `OutlinePass` (extending `PostProcessPass`) into the FrameGraph color chain.
**Priority 200**: Executes after core 3D rasterization and before final screen presentation.

blocks.text: C. Core Engine Subsystems as IPlugin Features ([CoreFeatures.ts](../src/engine/render/features/CoreFeatures.ts))
In Retiam, internal renderer passes are treated as first-class plugins implementing `IPlugin`:

items: **`ShadowFeature`** (Priority 10): Renders 2048x2048 light-space depth shadow maps.
**`RaytraceFeature`** (Priority 20): Executes the hardware-accelerated Monte Carlo path tracer when enabled.
**`PPLLPrepareFeature`** (Priority 30): Allocates Per-Pixel Linked List (PPLL) head pointer and fragment buffers for Order-Independent Transparency.
**`MainRasterFeature`** (Priority 50): Rasterizes opaque 3D meshes, 2D vector shapes, SDF text, and analytical Béziers.
**`PPLLCompositeFeature`** (Priority 70): Resolves and blends transparent fragments in depth order.

blocks.text: D. [FrameFeedbackFeature](../src/engine/render/passes/FeedbackPass.ts) (Temporal Feedback & Motion Trails)
An `IPlugin` feature providing ping-pong feedback textures across frames for phosphorescent trails, visual echoes, and generative feedback loops. Enabled via `scene.enableFrameFeedback()`.

blocks.text: 7. Best Practices for Plugin Authors

items: **Zero-Allocation Render Loops**:

blocks.text: Always pre-allocate temporary vectors, matrices, and scratch variables outside `scene.always()` to eliminate Garbage Collection stutter at 60/120 FPS.

items: **Implement `dispose()`**:

blocks.text: Always clean up GPU buffers (`buffer.destroy()`), remove passes, and cancel active listeners when the plugin is uninstalled.

items: **Respect the Open-Closed Principle**:

blocks.text: Never require end-users or other plugins to modify `ModelGeometry.ts`, `Domains.ts`, or `common.wgsl`. Rely on `IPlugin`, `ChunkRegistry`, and FrameGraph injection instead.

items: **Fluid Chaining**:

blocks.text: Ensure `scene.use(...)` returns `this` to allow clean chainable configuration:

items: **Use `priority` for ordering**:

blocks.text: Core engine features use priority 0–50. Plugin features default to 100. Use higher values (200+) for post-processing that should run after core raster.
